Recovery: --socket PATH promote GROUP --node NODE --accept-data-loss
Select one readable recovered population when no automatic candidate exists.
Direct commands are sent to the specified Meta node as one line.
Lavik Admin: --socket /path/to/admin.sock fleet-list, fleet-add NAME
IP:PORT, fleet-status NAME, fleet-operations NAME, fleet-failover NAME
GROUP, fleet-replica-add NAME GROUP NODE ENDPOINT, or
fleet-replica-remove NAME GROUP NODE. These share the Admin catalog.
Cluster setup: fleet-hosts, fleet-releases [PAGE], fleet-plan BASE64URL_JSON,
fleet-deploy REVIEW_TOKEN NAME, fleet-follower-plan NAME BASE64URL_JSON,
fleet-follower-deploy NAME REVIEW_TOKEN. Use --timeout-ms 600000 for
SSH host checks. The packaged lavik-admin ctl helper accepts JSON files.
status reports that node's state; cluster-status discovers the leader
and reports cluster readiness. cluster-create creates the v1 multi-
Data, multi-Group topology and returns after its Genesis commit. Use
cluster-status to follow creation and serving readiness. Options may
precede
any local cluster command.
Durability recovery uses: abortop ID, archiveoperations SEQ..., then
exportoperations and pruneoperations SEQ....
Exit status is 0 for an OK reply, 2 for an ERR reply, and 1 for a
local, connection, TLS, or malformed-protocol failure.
cluster-status exits 0 for READY, 2 for NOT READY, 3 for RETRYABLE,
and 1 for fatal errors. TCP discovery requires mTLS or explicit
--allow-plaintext-admin; --json applies only to cluster-status.
cluster-create exits 0 after Genesis commit, 2 for an explicit
Meta rejection, 3 for a possibly committed interruption/timeout, and
1 for local manifest, confirmation, or pre-mutation transport errors.
failover exits 0 after request commit, 2 for an explicit rejection,
3 for an uncertain proposal outcome, and 1 for local/transport errors known to occur before submission.
